_meta.semantics: covers_syllabus_refs is an index of the objectives a stage is principally associated with; coverage is claimed only through _syllabus_items + covers_items, and only as far as coverage_check.py confirms.

_items_source.document: AAT Level 3 Diploma in Accounting qualification specification (Qualification Number 603/6337/X), Version 5.12, published 1 September 2026, fetched live from aat.org.uk 2026-09-27, itemised in full against AAT's own scope-of-content numbering for each of the four mandatory units. VAT and payroll figures in the Tax Processes for Businesses unit are the 2026/27 UK tax year's rates, thresholds and statutory payment amounts, fetched live from HMRC (gov.uk) and current payroll-rates publishers on 2026-09-27.
_items_source.version: Version 5.12 (published 1 September 2026), the current version linked from aat.org.uk/deliver/qualifications/specifications-outlines, itemised 2026-09-27; the Tax Processes for Businesses unit follows AAT's FA2025 (Finance Act 2025) edition, the version current for assessments at the time this course was built, with UK tax/payroll figures for the 2026/27 tax year fetched live on the same date.
_items_source.numbering: AAT's own scope-of-content numbering, which restarts at 1 for each of the four units. This course prefixes each reference with the unit's initials to keep every code unique across the qualification: BA (Business Awareness), FA (Financial Accounting: Preparing Financial Statements), MA (Management Accounting Techniques), TAX (Tax Processes for Businesses) -- e.g. FA5.2 is AAT's own topic 5.2 within Financial Accounting: Preparing Financial Statements's learning outcome 5.

_syllabus_items.title: Organisational structure and governance: functional/divisional/matrix structures, span of control, centralised vs decentralised, operational/managerial/strategic levels, the finance function's role, types of risk and how they are managed

_syllabus_items.title: Sustainability: the triple bottom line (social, ecological, economic/financial), long-term stakeholder perspectives, responsible resource management and the accountant's public interest duty
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Business Awareness -- LO2 Understand the impact of the external and internal environment on businesses

_syllabus_items.title: The fundamental principles of the ethical code: integrity, objectivity, professional behaviour, professional competence and due care, confidentiality, professional scepticism, and safeguards against threats

_syllabus_items.title: Ethical conflicts: how they arise, resolving them, disciplinary and legal consequences, and how to report unethical behaviour

_syllabus_items.title: Money laundering: placement, layering and integration, the offences of tipping off and failure to disclose, and reporting suspicious activity

_syllabus_items.title: New technologies in accounting: automation, AI and machine learning, blockchain, e-filing/e-signing, data analytics, outsourcing/offshoring, and cloud accounting

_syllabus_items.title: Data protection and security: the UK GDPR principles, the impact of a data breach, information security controls and cybersecurity
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Business Awareness -- LO4 Understand the impact of new technologies in accounting and risks associated with data security

_syllabus_items.title: Information requirements and big data: qualities of good information, the three organisational levels, the five Vs of big data, and its benefits, limitations and sources

_syllabus_items.title: Visualising information: choosing an appropriate chart/diagram/table/matrix, identifying patterns and anomalies, and communicating dashboards to non-technical stakeholders
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Business Awareness -- LO5 Communicate information to stakeholders

_syllabus_items.title: Choosing an appropriate communication method: matching the medium to the stakeholder, ensuring validity and confidentiality
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Business Awareness -- LO5 Communicate information to stakeholders

_syllabus_items.title: The primary users of final accounts: existing and potential investors, lenders, and other creditors, and how each uses the accounts
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Financial Accounting: Preparing Financial Statements -- LO1 Understand the accounting principles underlying final accounts preparation

_syllabus_items.title: The framework of accounting: the accruals, going concern, business entity, materiality, consistency, prudence and money measurement principles
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Financial Accounting: Preparing Financial Statements -- LO1 Understand the accounting principles underlying final accounts preparation

_syllabus_items.title: Qualities of useful financial information: the fundamental characteristics (relevance, faithful representation) and enhancing characteristics (comparability, verifiability, timeliness, understandability)
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Financial Accounting: Preparing Financial Statements -- LO1 Understand the accounting principles underlying final accounts preparation

_syllabus_items.title: The accounting equation: its importance, the effect of transactions on capital/assets/liabilities, and calculating any element from the other two

_syllabus_items.title: Classifying ledger accounts: non-current and current assets (tangible/intangible), non-current and current liabilities, equity, income and expenses

_syllabus_items.title: Books of prime entry and ledger accounting: the daybooks, the general ledger vs memorandum ledgers, and control accounts (receivables, payables, wages and salaries, VAT)
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Financial Accounting: Preparing Financial Statements -- LO2 Understand the principles of advanced double-entry bookkeeping

_syllabus_items.title: Financial period end routines: balancing off accounts by classification, verifying balances, and determining whether transactions are genuine and valid
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Financial Accounting: Preparing Financial Statements -- LO2 Understand the principles of advanced double-entry bookkeeping

_syllabus_items.title: The importance of prior authority for capital expenditure: why it is needed and who should give it
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Financial Accounting: Preparing Financial Statements -- LO3 Implement procedures for the acquisition and disposal of non-current assets

_syllabus_items.title: Capital vs revenue expenditure under IAS 16: cost, useful life, residual value, depreciable amount and carrying amount; what can and cannot be included in cost
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Financial Accounting: Preparing Financial Statements -- LO3 Implement procedures for the acquisition and disposal of non-current assets

_syllabus_items.title: Recording acquisitions and disposals: the non-current asset register, part-exchange, and gains/losses on disposal (including VAT treatment by registration status)

_syllabus_items.title: Calculating depreciation: the straight-line method (with/without residual value, full year or pro-rata) and the diminishing (reducing) balance method
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Financial Accounting: Preparing Financial Statements -- LO4 Prepare and record depreciation calculations

_syllabus_items.title: Recording depreciation: in the non-current asset register and the general ledger (journal entries), and reconciling the two
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Financial Accounting: Preparing Financial Statements -- LO4 Prepare and record depreciation calculations

_syllabus_items.title: Accruals and prepayments of income and expenditure: calculating and recording the adjustment, and reversing the prior period's accrual/prepayment
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Financial Accounting: Preparing Financial Statements -- LO5 Record period end adjustments

_syllabus_items.title: Irrecoverable debts and allowances for doubtful receivables: writing off, recovering a previously written-off debt, and specific vs general allowances
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Financial Accounting: Preparing Financial Statements -- LO5 Record period end adjustments

_syllabus_items.title: Recording inventory under IAS 2: valuing at the lower of cost and net realisable value on an item-by-item basis, and the journal for closing inventory
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Financial Accounting: Preparing Financial Statements -- LO5 Record period end adjustments

_syllabus_items.title: Considerations when recording period end adjustments: their effect on reported results, and responding appropriately to time and reporting pressure
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Financial Accounting: Preparing Financial Statements -- LO5 Record period end adjustments

_syllabus_items.title: The initial trial balance: normal debit/credit balances, its purpose and limitations, and correcting errors with and without a suspense account
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Financial Accounting: Preparing Financial Statements -- LO6 Produce and extend the trial balance

_syllabus_items.title: The adjusted trial balance: placing closing inventory, accruals/prepayments, error corrections, depreciation, irrecoverable debts/allowances and disposals
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Financial Accounting: Preparing Financial Statements -- LO6 Produce and extend the trial balance

_syllabus_items.title: The extended trial balance (ETB): completing the profit-or-loss and financial-position columns and balancing off to find the profit or loss for the period
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Financial Accounting: Preparing Financial Statements -- LO6 Produce and extend the trial balance

_syllabus_items.title: The sole trader's statement of profit or loss and statement of financial position: purpose, terminology and preparation (net assets presentation)
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Financial Accounting: Preparing Financial Statements -- LO7 Produce financial statements for sole traders and partnerships

_syllabus_items.title: The sole trader's capital account: accounting for drawings (cash, goods, services), capital injections and the period's profit or loss
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Financial Accounting: Preparing Financial Statements -- LO7 Produce financial statements for sole traders and partnerships

_syllabus_items.title: The partnership's statement of profit or loss and appropriation account: interest on capital/drawings, salaries and the residual profit share by profit-sharing ratio
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Financial Accounting: Preparing Financial Statements -- LO7 Produce financial statements for sole traders and partnerships

_syllabus_items.title: The partnership's statement of financial position: partners' capital and current accounts, and preparing both
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Financial Accounting: Preparing Financial Statements -- LO7 Produce financial statements for sole traders and partnerships

_syllabus_items.title: Calculating profitability ratios: ROCE, gross profit margin, net profit margin and the expense/sales revenue percentage
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Financial Accounting: Preparing Financial Statements -- LO8 Interpret financial statements using profitability ratios

_syllabus_items.title: Interpreting profitability ratios: why they matter for planning/decisions/control, what causes them to change, and comparing them meaningfully
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Financial Accounting: Preparing Financial Statements -- LO8 Interpret financial statements using profitability ratios

_syllabus_items.title: Identifying missing figures from incomplete records: reconstructing the receivables/payables control accounts, the VAT control account and the bank account
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Financial Accounting: Preparing Financial Statements -- LO9 Prepare accounting records from incomplete information

_syllabus_items.title: Mark-up and margin: the difference between them, and using each to calculate missing figures via cost of sales
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Financial Accounting: Preparing Financial Statements -- LO9 Prepare accounting records from incomplete information

_syllabus_items.title: Assessing the reasonableness of figures when information is incomplete, and why an actual and a calculated balance can differ
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Financial Accounting: Preparing Financial Statements -- LO9 Prepare accounting records from incomplete information

_syllabus_items.title: The purpose of costing, budgeting and internal reporting, and the importance of providing accurate information
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Management Accounting Techniques -- LO1 Understand the purpose and use of management accounting within organisations

_syllabus_items.title: Classifying costs: fixed, variable and semi-variable by behaviour; direct and indirect by element; product and period costs
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Management Accounting Techniques -- LO2 Use techniques required for dealing with costs

_syllabus_items.title: Materials costing: calculating the cost of issues and closing inventory using FIFO, LIFO and AVCO, and their effect on profit and inventory valuation
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Management Accounting Techniques -- LO2 Use techniques required for dealing with costs

_syllabus_items.title: Labour costing: direct vs indirect labour, and calculating labour cost including overtime premium
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Management Accounting Techniques -- LO2 Use techniques required for dealing with costs

_syllabus_items.title: Overhead allocation and absorption: allocation vs apportionment, apportionment bases, calculating absorption rates, and accounting for under/over absorption
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Management Accounting Techniques -- LO2 Use techniques required for dealing with costs

_syllabus_items.title: Marginal vs absorption costing: preparing statements under each method, and reconciling the difference in reported profit
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Management Accounting Techniques -- LO3 Attribute costs according to organisational requirements

_syllabus_items.title: Budgeting: the purpose of budgets, fixed and flexible budgets, and preparing functional budgets
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Management Accounting Techniques -- LO4 Investigate deviations from budgets

_syllabus_items.title: Variance analysis: material price/usage, labour rate/efficiency, variable and fixed overhead, and sales price/volume variances, and interpreting their causes
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Management Accounting Techniques -- LO4 Investigate deviations from budgets

_syllabus_items.title: Spreadsheet techniques for management accounting: formulas and functions, sorting/filtering, pivot tables, charts and validating data
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Management Accounting Techniques -- LO5 Use spreadsheet techniques to provide management accounting information

_syllabus_items.title: Cost-volume-profit analysis: contribution, calculating the breakeven point (units and sales value), margin of safety and target profit
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Management Accounting Techniques -- LO6 Use management accounting techniques to support short-term decision making

_syllabus_items.title: Limiting factor analysis: identifying the scarce resource and ranking products by contribution per unit of limiting factor to find the optimal mix
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Management Accounting Techniques -- LO6 Use management accounting techniques to support short-term decision making

_syllabus_items.title: Relevant costing: distinguishing relevant from irrelevant costs, and applying this to make-or-buy and discontinuation decisions
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Management Accounting Techniques -- LO6 Use management accounting techniques to support short-term decision making

_syllabus_items.title: Cash flow forecasting: the difference between profit and cash, and preparing a cash flow forecast
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Management Accounting Techniques -- LO7 Understand principles of cash management

_syllabus_items.title: Managing cash surpluses and deficits, and working-capital measures (current ratio, quick ratio, receivables/payables/inventory days)
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Management Accounting Techniques -- LO7 Understand principles of cash management

_syllabus_items.title: The UK tax system: the main taxes and their purposes, HMRC's role, how tax legislation is made and changed, and the impact of avoidance vs evasion
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Tax Processes for Businesses -- LO1 Understand the UK tax system and legislation

_syllabus_items.title: VAT principles: VAT as a consumption tax, taxable/exempt/zero-rated/outside-the-scope supplies, and the current VAT rates
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Tax Processes for Businesses -- LO2 Understand the principles of VAT and VAT registration/deregistration

_syllabus_items.title: VAT registration and deregistration: the registration threshold, mandatory vs voluntary registration, the deregistration threshold and its VAT implications
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Tax Processes for Businesses -- LO2 Understand the principles of VAT and VAT registration/deregistration

_syllabus_items.title: Calculating VAT: output tax and input tax, when input tax cannot be recovered, and adjusting for credit notes/prompt payment discounts
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Tax Processes for Businesses -- LO3 Understand how to prepare accurate VAT returns

_syllabus_items.title: Preparing and submitting the VAT return: the return's boxes, deadlines, records to keep, and the consequences of non-compliance
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Tax Processes for Businesses -- LO3 Understand how to prepare accurate VAT returns

_syllabus_items.title: Using tax documentation and legislation: the types of documentation used, accessing current information, and applying it to specific situations
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Tax Processes for Businesses -- LO4 Understand the use of relevant tax documentation and legislation

_syllabus_items.title: Communicating VAT and tax information: choosing the right method for HMRC vs for clients, and the importance of accuracy and timeliness
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Tax Processes for Businesses -- LO5 Communicate VAT and tax information

_syllabus_items.title: Payroll: the documents used, the components of gross pay, statutory and voluntary deductions (income tax via PAYE, employee NIC), and calculating net pay
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Tax Processes for Businesses -- LO6 Understand payroll administration

_syllabus_items.title: Statutory payments (SSP, SMP, SPP), Real Time Information (RTI) submission, and payment deadlines to HMRC
_syllabus_items.topic_area: Tax Processes for Businesses -- LO6 Understand payroll administration
